the proposed method is able to achieve a higher classification accuracy than other methods.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new variational EM method for DSBNs with cDBM as inference model, and we show that the cDBM model can be used for parameter estimation without computing the partition function, which is intractable in general, but is approximated with contrastive divergence in our experiments.

the proposed algorithm is a new learning scheme of DSBNs that is capable of representing the dependencies among the latent variables in the generative model, and can achieve comparable performance with the mean field approximation method and the wake sleep algorithm.

the VEM algorithm with the conditional deep Boltmann machine is able to learn DSBNs with more complex latent variable dependencies and can be accelerated by using the contrastive divergence algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed VEM learning algorithm with the cDBM inference model can achieve comparable performance to that of the wake sleep algorithm with the DBM model.
the proposed method outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy and computational efficiency.
the cDBM is a powerful and flexible tool to model complex dependencies among latent factors in deep sigmoid belief networks.
